@copilot Update this PR directly with the user's requested cleanup: use telemetryConfig for the paired telemetry JVM setting and metadataConfig assignments, and limit the migration to clear, simple-to-review changes.

Remove both Cassandra migrations from this PR: instrumentation/cassandra/cassandra-4.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts and instrumentation/cassandra/cassandra-4.4/javaagent/build.gradle.kts. Restore only this PR's changes in those files relative to the PR's intended base, preserving upstream work. Their helper-generated shaded-driver executions and custom classpath substitutions are too involved for this batch. Do not replace them with other modules or try to retain the old 40-file count. The other 38 files contain direct named test variants and are the intended remaining scope.

In the remaining build files, replace paired jvmArgs("-Dkey=value") / systemProperty("metadataConfig", "key=value") declarations with telemetryConfig("key", "value"), importing io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.gradle.telemetryConfig. Elasticsearch transport 5.0 is the simple reference example. Inspect the existing helper implementation in conventions/src/main/kotlin/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/gradle/TestSuiteExecutions.kt: it sets the JVM property and accumulates the metadata profile. Convert shared and variant settings coherently when a metadata profile combines several properties, so inherited settings and ordering are preserved rather than overwritten by mixed helper/manual metadata handling. Preserve the exact effective properties, defaults, and metadata labels. Do not add metadata to flags or regression tasks that had no metadata profile just to use the helper.

Keep the executions DSL migration otherwise mechanical and easy to review. Preserve all existing task names, source suites, filters/includes/excludes, default-only settings, shared JVM configuration, metadata profiles, dependencies, toolchain/latest-dependency behavior, and check coverage. Keep unrelated global policies where needed. Avoid new abstractions, helper functions, convention changes, production-code changes, or new coverage. The earlier migration already retained these behaviors; do not broaden the work. Read the applicable repository build instructions and existing javaagent executions / telemetryConfig examples.

Run relevant narrow spotlessApply directly and appropriate documented Gradle validation. Do not use spotlessCheck as a preliminary step, clean, --rerun-tasks, or disabled caches. Report real environment blockers accurately. Keep the existing draft PR state, and do not create a separate PR.

@copilot Update this PR directly with the user's requested further simplification, including other Gradle files in this PR where the same simplification preserves behavior. Keep the current 38-file scope and do not reintroduce either Cassandra migration.

Use instrumentation/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-transport-5.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts as the reference. Replace its separate tasks block and deeply nested testing block with testing.suites.named<JvmTestSuite>("test") { executions { configureEach { jvmArgs("--add-opens=java.base/java.nio=ALL-UNNAMED"); jvmArgs("-XX:+IgnoreUnrecognizedVMOptions") }; register("Experimental") { telemetryConfig("otel.instrumentation.elasticsearch.experimental-span-attributes", "true") } } }. Keep the current short comment explaining the JDK argument. The real code should use normal multiline Kotlin formatting, not the semicolon-packed illustration in this paragraph. The executions helper already wires the default and variant Test tasks into check, so the explicit check dependency is redundant in this file.

Apply the same clear simplifications to the other remaining build.gradle.kts files changed by this PR: flatten the default-suite declaration, keep testing declarations at project level instead of inside tasks, and move shared test settings into executions.configureEach only when that scopes them to exactly the same existing executions. Preserve baseline-only filters/configuration on the baseline task rather than sharing them with variants. Remove redundant task/check boilerplate only where the DSL already supplies all of its dependencies. Keep explicit check dependencies for additional source suites not covered by an executions block. Retain global Test policies where other suites/tasks need them, and preserve all-task Testcontainers service registration when applicable. Do not broaden this into outside-PR cleanup or add abstractions.

Preserve all 51 named variants, task names, source suites, dependencies, filters/includes/excludes, JVM/system properties, metadata profiles and ordering, default behavior, check coverage, and latest-dependency/toolchain constraints. Keep telemetryConfig for the paired setting/profile declarations. When collapsing shared settings, remove duplicate raw JVM declarations for a property only after confirming the same effective setting remains on every required execution. Do not add metadata to unlabeled flags or regression tasks. Read the existing TestSuiteExecutions implementation and applicable repository build instructions before editing.

Run narrow relevant spotlessApply directly and documented Gradle validation of the affected tasks and check wiring. Do not use clean, --rerun-tasks, cache bypasses, or preliminary spotlessCheck. Preserve the draft PR state and do not create another PR.

replies.body: Applied in 6aaa7f37. Flattened the default-suite declarations across the existing 38 files, moved shared settings into execution configuration where appropriate, and kept baseline-only filters and global test policies scoped as before. Both Cassandra files remain excluded.

@copilot Update this PR directly with the user-requested remaining shared-test configuration cleanup and its supporting repository guidance. This supersedes the earlier instruction to preserve global Testcontainers registration even when one executions block covers all tasks. The user clarified: "This guidance is only for the purpose of avoiding fine grained messiness in the build files" and requested updating the guidance and this PR when moving the shared block avoids that messiness.

Move the five existing denyUnsafe disablement blocks into the existing test suite executions.configureEach blocks in instrumentation/couchbase/couchbase-3.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts, instrumentation/couchbase/couchbase-3.1/javaagent/build.gradle.kts, instrumentation/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-transport-5.3/javaagent/build.gradle.kts, instrumentation/hystrix-1.4/javaagent/build.gradle.kts, and instrumentation/jaxrs/jaxrs-3.0/jaxrs-3.0-resteasy-6.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts. Keep the condition if (otelProps.denyUnsafe) { enabled = false } rather than unconditionally resetting enabled on other runs. These modules currently have only main/test source directories and the default suite with its registered variants.

Move the four existing usesService(gradle.sharedServices.registrations["testcontainersBuildService"].service) declarations into executions.configureEach for the test suite in both Couchbase builds above, instrumentation/lettuce/lettuce-4.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts, and instrumentation/opensearch/opensearch-java-3.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts. Apply service registration once to the entire suite execution family, including container-free variants, without task-by-task/container-use filtering. It must continue to cover every currently covered Test execution. Combine it with existing common configuration instead of declaring multiple executions blocks or duplicating per-variant settings. Remove empty tasks blocks and unneeded withType<Test>().configureEach blocks. Preserve OpenSearch baseline-only filters on the baseline task and all other task-specific settings.

Update .github/instructions/instrumentation-gradle.instructions.md and the directly related Testcontainers/shared-test-configuration guidance in .github/agents/knowledge/gradle-conventions.md. Explain the invariant concisely: keep common configuration, including Testcontainers scheduling, in one shared declaration rather than fine-grained per-task/per-variant selection; executions.configureEach is appropriate when the selected suite and its variants cover the relevant tasks; retain tasks.withType<Test>().configureEach for genuinely project-wide settings spanning other suites or independent Test tasks. Do not insist on a global block merely to include container-free variants already covered by the suite block. Preserve the requirement to register the build service for every Testcontainers-using execution and to inspect actual test sources rather than infer usage from dependencies. Reconcile the knowledge article's currently contradictory direction to register only specific tasks and its "Do not over-apply" advice with the user's clarified intent. Keep the edits scoped to these two guidance files and the seven existing PR build files, not a repository-wide rollout or convention implementation change.

Preserve the PR's 38 javaagent build-file scope, all 51 named variants, task names, source suites, test classes/classpaths, properties and metadata profiles/order, filters, default behavior, toolchain/latest-dependency constraints, check wiring, and Testcontainers concurrency coverage. Keep both Cassandra files excluded. The only added files in the PR should be the two guidance files. No new abstractions, per-task container inventories, production-code changes, or additional test variants. Read TestSuiteExecutions.kt and the relevant guidance before editing. Run narrow relevant spotlessApply directly and the repository Markdown fixer for the changed Markdown files, then documented Gradle validation covering the seven modules and their tasks/check wiring. Do not run clean, preliminary spotlessCheck, --rerun-tasks, or disable caches. Report real validation blockers accurately. Preserve the existing draft PR state and do not create another PR.

replies.body: Moved the shared test policies and Testcontainers service registrations into the suite executions, and updated both guidance files. Seven-module `check` and targeted `spotlessApply` passed. Commit: `1eb6b5ca`. The Markdown fixer was unavailable because neither `mise` nor Flint is installed.

@copilot Update this PR directly with the user-approved executions DSL extension and migrate its five remaining baseline-only test blocks. The user asked "What if we extend the DSL?" and invoked /cloud for the proposed configureDefault entry. Implement configureDefault rather than moving baseline-only settings into configureEach or introducing a new default test task. This is a scoped extension of the existing PR, not a repository-wide migration.

In conventions/src/main/kotlin/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/gradle/TestSuiteExecutions.kt, add configureDefault(action: Action<Test>) using a separate collection of default-only actions, consistent with the existing configureEach actions. Collect the whole executions block before applying configuration. For each existing suite target, apply common configureEach actions first, then configureDefault actions, regardless of their declaration order. Apply only common and variant actions to registered variants. Keep task configuration lazy, including an already-realized default task, and support named suites without hardcoding "test". Do not create another Test task, compilation, classpath, or source set for the default. Preserve existing task binding, check wiring, duplicate-block/suffix behavior, and variant laziness. Keep the change small, with no general task registry or new abstractions. Add concise current-behavior API documentation where useful.

Move the five existing baseline-only test configurations into configureDefault inside their existing executions blocks: instrumentation/netty/netty-4.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts excludes Netty40ConnectionSpanTest and Netty40ClientSslTest; instrumentation/opensearch/opensearch-java-3.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts excludes OpenSearchQuerySanitizationDisabledTest and OpenSearchQuerySanitizationDisabledJsonbTest; instrumentation/spring/spring-webflux/spring-webflux-5.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts excludes **/server/**; instrumentation/opentelemetry-extension-annotations-1.0/javaagent/build.gradle.kts applies its opentelemetry-annotations.exclude-methods JVM argument; instrumentation/opentelemetry-instrumentation-annotations-1.16/javaagent/build.gradle.kts applies its opentelemetry-instrumentation-annotations.exclude-methods JVM argument. Preserve the exact filters/property values and their baseline-only scope. In particular, their named variants must not receive the exclusions or flat-property arguments; declarative-config variants retain their separate YAML configuration path. Keep common JVM settings and Testcontainers service registration in configureEach, and retain every variant-specific setting. Remove the obsolete baseline test blocks and empty tasks wrappers; preserve both annotation modules' compileTestJava -parameters configuration.

Add focused regression coverage in conventions/src/test/kotlin/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/gradle/TestSuiteExecutionsTest.kt for default-only configuration isolation from variants, common-before-default precedence independent of declaration order, default-only filters/JVM properties, named-suite isolation, lazy configuration and already-realized defaults, and unchanged task/check binding without an extra default execution. Reuse the existing helpers and test patterns, and do not broaden this into unrelated convention tests.

Update the directly related execution/baseline guidance in .github/instructions/instrumentation-gradle.instructions.md and .github/agents/knowledge/gradle-conventions.md to distinguish configureEach for shared settings, configureDefault for an execution family's baseline-only settings, and register for named variants. Keep tasks.test appropriate for standalone single-test-task projects, and preserve the clarified suite-wide Testcontainers scheduling guidance. Keep documentation concise and in those existing files rather than adding new documents.

Preserve the existing 38 javaagent build-file scope, all 51 variants, task names, filters/includes/excludes, properties and metadata profiles/order, classpaths, source suites, dependencies, default behavior, latest-dependency/toolchain constraints, check coverage, and Testcontainers concurrency coverage. Keep both Cassandra builds excluded. Beyond the current PR files, only the execution helper and its existing test file should become changed files. Run narrow relevant spotlessApply directly, the focused TestSuiteExecutionsTest class, and documented Gradle validation for the five migrated modules and their check/variant wiring. Use the repository Markdown fixer for the changed guidance when available, and report any missing tooling accurately. Do not use clean, preliminary spotlessCheck, --rerun-tasks, or cache bypasses. Preserve the existing draft PR state and do not create another PR.
